objection: Retargeting returns over 2x on the platform. Cutting it is madness.
response: The platform counts 35 customers per $1,000; switching it off in randomly chosen regions lost about 1.7 (at most 14). Most of what it claims would have bought anyway. Cutting it is worth $150k a year (at least $31k).
what would change our view: A repeat test in peak season showing a larger loss

objection: Give us more budget and we will grow faster.
response: Volume would grow, profit would not: the last $200k of the $2M brings back $0.91 per dollar and another $200k would bring back $0.43. The model's profit peaks near $1.8M.
what would change our view: Tests showing an untested channel earns well above $1 per dollar at the margin

objection: These are model numbers. How do I know the gain is real?
response: Part of the plan rests on experiments, part on the model. The experiment-backed moves are made in full; increases we cannot yet prove ($151k) are held as a reserve until tested. The pessimistic case is still $409k a year better than last year's split.
evidence: Causal for tested lines, model for the rest
what would change our view: A quarterly read-out below the pessimistic case

objection: LinkedIn lookalikes bring more leads for the same money. Switch.
response: They bring 12% more leads per dollar but 35% fewer qualified leads. The sales team would work more leads to win fewer customers.
what would change our view: A longer test showing qualified leads per dollar at least level

objection: Programmatic display gives us some of the cheapest leads in B2.
response: Programmatic display leads cost $77 (number 2 cheapest) but only 1.8% become customers, so each customer costs $4,408, against $1,378 through LinkedIn. Cost per lead is the wrong measure.
what would change our view: Better lead scoring that lifts its conversion rate

objection: We cannot trust any of this: the tracking keeps breaking.
response: The checks found 5 problems, all now flagged in the data. Budget decisions use the CRM and randomised tests, not platform pixels, so a broken pixel cannot move the budget.
what would change our view: A break in the CRM itself (not yet covered by the checks)

objection: Cutting B2 advertising will starve sales.
response: B2 already produces about 41 qualified leads a week against a team that can work 40. Ads beyond that buy leads nobody calls. Extra capacity, not extra ads, is what grows B2: the model values lifting the limit at up to $409k a year.
what would change our view: Sales hiring or faster lead handling
